collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A very old villager is baffled by a water beetle walking upside down: ask how it works, or just watch it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is very old now, and some of the young villagers seem to expect (subject.him/her) to know everything already. (subject.He/she) doesn't. Today (subject.he/she) is crouched by the stream, watching a water beetle walk upside down on the underside of the surface, and (subject.he/she) is just as baffled and delighted as (subject.he/she) would have been at six.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) doesn't need to know how it works. (subject.He/she) just watches the beetle go about its upside-down business, round and round. (young_villager), a young villager passing by, stops, curious, and crouches beside (subject.him/her). They watch together in silence. (subject) thinks the best thing about getting old is that the world still has beetles like this in it.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (subject) grabs the nearest passing villager, (friend), and makes (subject.him/her) look. "How does it DO that?" (friend) has no idea. They both watch it for a long time. (friend) goes to fetch (scientist), a scientist. (scientist) isn't sure either. (subject) is delighted that nobody knows. "Good," (subject.he/she) says. "Something to find out."
